results.question: who can audit my soroban contract
results.answer: Several vetted audit firms can audit your Soroban contract [1][2][3][4][17]. Halborn offers full-stack blockchain security including audits and pentests [1], while OtterSec has a deep Soroban and Stellar track record [4]. Runtime Verification provides formal methods verification tooling and audits for Soroban [3], Certora offers prover-based formal verification extended to Soroban contracts [2], and Veridise provides formal verification and audits including work on Soroban core [17]. You can also find audit history and expert recommendations on the Stellar Security Portal [6].

results.question: tell me about Blend
results.answer: Blend is a lending and borrowing protocol (money market) on Stellar Soroban where anyone can deploy permissionless, isolated lending pools [2]. Suppliers earn yield by depositing assets like USDC, XLM and EURC, while borrowers take over-collateralized loans, making it the base lending and yield primitive other Stellar DeFi apps build on [2]. Blend is created by Script3 and has been audited by Certora, OtterSec, and Code4rena [8][12][13]. The protocol is preparing to release V2 and launched a $125K security audit competition in February 2025 [10], with the active v2 contracts repository last updated on 2026-10-26 [15].

results.question: open-source repos for zk proofs on Soroban
results.answer: Soroban-ZK-Std is a Stellar Protocol 25 ZK standard library for Soroban smart contracts covering CAP-0074 (BN254) and CAP-0075 (Poseidon/Poseidon2) host functions, written in Rust with active development as of October 2026 [25]. Fog-of-chess verifies every move with a zero-knowledge proof on Stellar, with players committing piece positions on-chain and each move proving legality in ZK without revealing which piece moved [20]. KALIEN uses RISC Zero proofs to verify deterministic gameplay tapes before rewards are minted on-chain [21]. LumenShade, an SCF submission, planned to implement ZK circuits in Circom or Noir and integrate a Circom verifier in Soroban for a privacy layer [14].

results.question: what is SEP-41
results.answer: SEP-41 is the Soroban Token Interface standard [6]. It defines a token standard for fully customizable contract tokens that implement the SEP-41 specification, with their own storage and logic, and can be held by both regular accounts and contract accounts without requiring trustlines [7]. The standard was created on 2023-09-22 and is currently in Draft status as of version 0.5.2 (updated 2026-08-24), authored by Jonathan Jove, Siddharth Suresh, Simon Chow, and Leigh McCulloch [6].

results.question: how does the Stellar consensus protocol work
results.answer: The Stellar Consensus Protocol (SCP) is a proof of agreement protocol that distributes the monitoring and approval of transactions across many individual nodes instead of relying on a single authority [12][13]. It uses a federated Byzantine agreement (FBA) model where each node makes individual trust decisions called quorum slices that together determine system-level quorums, binding the system together [11]. Nodes reach consensus, apply a transaction set, and update the ledger every 5-7 seconds using Stellar Core, the program that keeps a common distributed ledger and engages in consensus to validate and process transactions [14].

results.question: what is a trustline
results.answer: A trustline is a ledger entry that allows a Stellar account to hold and trade a non-native asset issued by another account [14]. To receive or hold an asset on Stellar, an account must first create a trustline to that asset by setting a trust limit, which specifies the maximum amount of the asset the account is willing to hold [14]. Trustlines are managed through the ChangeTrust operation and can be created, updated, or deleted [14]. Projects like StellarTerm and MetaMask provide interfaces to manage trustlines, and protocols like Authline bundle trustline creation with authorization into a single transaction to simplify onboarding [2][4][7].
